gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Noto Sans Nabataean reads tall and open, its lowercase nearly as high as the capitals. Bevellier sits above it with a flat, stencil-cut look and tightly packed glyphs, so the two feel like a sharp cut-paper title over a plain sans that lets the words breathe.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundar: Graceful is Bevellier's first move, drawn as if with one pen tip and set with very tight spacing. Noto Sans Nag Mundari follows with lowercase that rivals its capitals, and next to the heading it feels brisk, modern and a touch looser in the joints.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-nandinagar: Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous and its lowercase big, with short ascenders. Noto Sans Nandinagari gives Bevellier, whose strokes look traced by a laser-etched line, a friendly, easygoing partner that never crowds the display letters.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-newa: Bevellier's crossbars are as fat as the stems they join, which gives its wide, squat-ascendered lowercase a stencil-cut look that is hard to miss. Bevellier handles the dramatic entrance, while Noto Sans Newa, with its open e, does the steady talking.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Bevellier has no hairlines and no swelling strokes, just flat, single-weight letters packed tightly together. And Noto Sans Nushu, with its towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke, brings a modern sans that stands tall beside it.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham has wide gaps in its e and bodies so tall that the lowercase looks bold. And Bevellier, with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye, lets that body text run on in a long, clean line when paragraphs pile up.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds the tails of its curves well back, so words settle into solid blocks instead of ragged skylines. Bevellier's stroke contrast is essentially zero.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-old-north-: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and tall, with terminals pointing outward like a pair of tongs. And Bevellier, whose w has no thick or thin strokes, feels slick and sophisticated beside that sturdy, approachable plain sans.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Bevellier cuts its letters flat like a stencil, with crossbars matching the stems in thickness and a high, wide lowercase with squat ascenders. Noto Sans Old Permic stays open and round beneath.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-old-persia: Noto Sans Old Persian reads lofty and open, its counters breathing into the white space around them. Noto Sans Old Persian handles the steady reading, while Bevellier, drawn as if with one pen tip, supplies the graceful, stencil-flat flourish.
